#ETH upcoming Glamsterdam upgrade, planned for 2026, is designed to improve fairness around MEV (Maximal Extractable Value) while continuing to strengthen the network’s efficiency and decentralization. Building on the success of the Fusaka upgrade, which lowered node operation costs, Glamsterdam will introduce parallel upgrades across Ethereum’s execution and consensus layers.
One of the key proposals is enshrined Proposer-Builder Separation (ePBS), which aims to reduce MEV concentration by separating block proposing from block building at the protocol level. Another important feature under discussion is block-level access lists, which could improve execution efficiency and reduce uncertainty for transactions. While the full feature set is still being finalized, development work has already started, signaling Ethereum’s long-term focus on scalability, fairness, and a healthier validator ecosystem.#ETH🔥🔥🔥🔥🔥🔥

#ETH 
At three in the morning, on the other end of the phone, a trembling voice from a female fan in Hangzhou, Xiao Yezi, said: "Mr. Ye, I have been liquidated, 500,000 U is gone, only 4,000 U left..."

The despair in her voice was truly palpable—I could tell she wasn't afraid of losing money, but rather of never being able to turn things around again. I looked through her trading records, and the problem was clear at a glance:

Chasing heights when the market rises, stubbornly holding on when it falls; seeing others make money, she goes all in; she talks about stopping losses but never acts on it.

This isn't trading cryptocurrencies; it's clearly gambling with her life. I didn't blame her, nor did I let her operate immediately; I just said: "Stop thinking about profits for now, first learn not to lose money."

I told her to take a week off, to review every losing trade thoroughly. A week later she told me: "I understand now, it's not the market that's losing, it's myself."

Ninety percent of her losses stemmed from two things: impatience and lack of discipline. So, I laid down two strict rules for her:

If a single trade loses more than 5%, close the position immediately; if she loses 10% in a day, stop trading for that day, no matter how tempting the market looks.

Next, I taught her a strategy to win steadily: only trade major currencies like BTC, ETH; only open positions at key support levels, setting stop-loss at 1.5% outside the price; for each trade, take out the principal after making 5% and continue with profits.

This way, she no longer feared making mistakes because losses were just earnings that had been retracted. Finally, I gave her a small task: use 4,000 U to divide into three small currencies, with the condition that large wallets are increasing their holdings, and the exchange balance is decreasing, indicating someone is accumulating.

Five months later, she sent me a screenshot, her account balance was 700,000 U. She said: "Mr. Ye, I'm no longer afraid of losses. I've not only made back what I lost but also earned an additional 200,000 U."

I laughed; she had transformed from a gambler into a planned trader.

Brothers, remember: there are no dead ends in the cryptocurrency world, just a fear of not learning from mistakes. What you lose isn't the market, but the greed for overnight riches.

Liquidation isn't scary; not waking up is fatal. There are many opportunities in the market; whether you can seize them depends on whether you're still alive.

If you want to turn things around, don't seek miracles; first, practice your basics well. Steadily earn your first 5%, and the subsequent 500%, 5000% will naturally follow. Not being able to earn is normal; surviving is winning.

title: 年轻人炒币热：一场被焦虑与骗局裹挟的冒险
subTitle:
#ETH #BTC 打开短视频，“00后炒币月入5万”的噱头不绝于耳；刷社交群，“百倍币抄底”的喊单与盈利截图轮番轰炸。如今不少年轻人涌入币圈，并非真懂区块链技术，而是被现实压力与暴富幻想推上了赌桌。
这股热潮的核心，是内卷时代的机会焦虑。高房价、慢增长的薪资、拥挤的就业赛道，让传统上升路径变得漫长。对手里没多少积蓄的年轻人来说，炒币“1元起投”的低门槛，恰好迎合了他们“以小博大”的心理——就像有人借贷10万冲“百倍币”，不过是想走条“快速翻盘”的捷径。而社交媒体的推波助澜，让这种焦虑更易扩散：KOL包装虚假行情、社群营造“错过即亏”的氛围，55%的Z世代甚至仅靠短视频获取炒币信息，却不知40%的推荐项目未经合规审计。
更值得警惕的是，炒币早已沦为针对性骗局。从网红“拉盘出货”收割散户，到熟人拉人头的传销式空气币，骗局套路不断翻新。有年轻人把结婚本金投入网红推荐的代币，4小时内就暴跌至近乎归零；也有人被“导师”暗示借网贷炒币，最终本金亏光还背上高额利息，连累家人还债。更讽刺的是，我国早已明确虚拟货币交易属非法金融活动，不受法律保护，但不少年轻人被“去中心化”“数字资产”的概念忽悠，忽视了背后的法律风险。
年轻人渴望财富增值本无可厚非，但炒币从来不是正解。当“新三金”理财、合规数字藏品等稳健路径已然存在，何必把青春赌在虚假泡沫上？真正的安全感，从来不是币价涨跌的数字游戏，而是合规框架下的踏实积累。远离炒币陷阱，守住本金底线，才是对未来最负责的选择。

#ETH #BTC  Opening short videos, the hype of "post-00s earning 50,000 a month from trading cryptocurrencies" is inescapable; scrolling through social groups, the barrage of calls for "bottom-fishing hundredfold coins" and profit screenshots is relentless. Nowadays, many young people are pouring into the cryptocurrency circle, not because they truly understand blockchain technology, but because they have been pushed to the gambling table by real-world pressures and fantasies of sudden wealth.
The core of this trend is the anxiety of opportunity in the era of involution. High housing prices, slow salary growth, and a crowded job market have made traditional upward paths lengthy. For young people who don't have much savings, the low entry barrier of "investing in cryptocurrencies from 1 yuan" just fits their mindset of "small bets for big returns"—just like some borrow 100,000 to chase after "hundredfold coins," simply looking for a shortcut to "quickly turn things around." Social media's amplification makes this anxiety spread more easily: KOLs package false market conditions, and communities create an atmosphere of "missing out means losing." 55% of Generation Z even rely solely on short videos to obtain cryptocurrency trading information, unaware that 40% of recommended projects have not undergone compliance audits.

title: BNB: Navigating the Evolving Crypto Landscape
subTitle:
Binance Coin (BNB), the native cryptocurrency of the Binance ecosystem, continues to hold a significant position in the broader crypto market, despite facing increased scrutiny and evolving regulatory environments. BNB was initially launched as an ERC-20 token on the Ethereum blockchain in 2017 but later migrated to its own blockchain, the Binance Chain, and subsequently became central to the Binance Smart Chain (now BNB Chain).
Core Utility and Ecosystem
BNB's primary utility lies within the vast Binance ecosystem. It offers users reduced trading fees on the Binance exchange, powers transactions on the BNB Chain (which supports a thriving DeFi and NFT space), and is used for participation in token sales on Binance Launchpad. The BNB Chain's compatibility with the Ethereum Virtual Machine (EVM) has made it a popular choice for developers looking for faster, cheaper transactions compared to Ethereum, fostering a robust decentralized application (dApp) ecosystem.
Performance and Market Position
Historically, BNB has shown strong performance, often moving in correlation with the broader market but also demonstrating independent strength driven by ecosystem developments and consistent token burns, which reduce its supply over time. Its market capitalization consistently places it among the top cryptocurrencies globally, reflecting the immense user base and trading volume on the Binance platform.
Challenges and Future Outlook
However, BNB operates in an increasingly complex regulatory landscape. Binance, the exchange behind BNB, has faced significant legal and regulatory challenges in various jurisdictions, leading to increased pressure on the BNB token. Compliance efforts, licensing issues, and regulatory crackdowns can introduce volatility and uncertainty.
Despite these headwinds, the ongoing development of the BNB Chain, its established utility, and Binance's continued global presence suggest that BNB will remain a key player. Its future trajectory will largely depend on Binance's ability to navigate regulatory hurdles, innovate its ecosystem, and maintain its competitive edge against other Layer 1 blockchains and centralized exchanges. Investors and users will be watching closely for how these factors play out in the coming months and years.#BTC #BNB_Market_Update #ETH $XRP

Hãy cùng tìm hiểu chuyện gì đã xảy ra, tại sao dễ bị lừa như vậy, và cách bảo vệ bản thân để không bao giờ rơi vào tình cảnh tương tự.
Chuyện gì đã xảy ra?Ngày 19-20/12/2025, nạn nhân rút 50 triệu USDT từ Binance về ví cá nhân.
Họ gửi một giao dịch thử nghiệm nhỏ (khoảng 50 USDT) đến địa chỉ ví đích (của chính mình hoặc người nhận đáng tin cậy) để kiểm tra.
Hacker ngay lập tức tạo một địa chỉ ví gần giống hệt:  Đầu giống 3-5 ký tự đầu, Cuối giống 4 ký tự cuối . Phần giữa khác, nhưng ví như MetaMask thường hiển thị kiểu "0xBaF...f8b5" (che dấu phần giữa), nên nhìn qua giống y chang.
Hacker gửi một lượng tiền nhỏ (dust) từ địa chỉ giả đến ví nạn nhân → địa chỉ giả này xuất hiện trong lịch sử giao dịch của nạn nhân.
Khi gửi số tiền lớn, nạn nhân copy địa chỉ từ lịch sử (thay vì nhập thủ công hoặc từ nguồn đáng tin), và... vô tình copy địa chỉ giả → 49,999,950 USDT bay thẳng vào tay hacker!
Hacker hành động siêu nhanh:  
Swap USDT sang DAI (stablecoin khó bị freeze hơn).  
Đổi sang ETH (khoảng 16.690 ETH).  
Đưa phần lớn vào Tornado Cash để rửa tiền, che giấu dấu vết.
Nạn nhân đã gửi thông điệp on-chain treo thưởng 1 triệu đô la nếu hacker trả lại 98% số tiền, và đe dọa kiện tụng. Nhưng crypto là "tiền đi một đường, không quay lại" – mất là mất thật!
Tại sao dễ bị lừa như vậy?Ví tiền điện tử thường hiển thị địa chỉ rút gọn (chỉ đầu + cuối + dấu ... ở giữa).  
Nhiều người chỉ kiểm tra đầu và cuối (vì nghĩ đủ an toàn).  
Copy từ lịch sử rất tiện, nhưng chính là điểm yếu lớn nhất.  
Hacker dùng bot tự động tạo địa chỉ giống và "đầu độc" hàng loạt ví, chỉ cần một người mắc bẫy là trúng đậm.
Năm 2025, tổng tiền crypto bị mất đã vượt 3,4 tỷ đô la, và các vụ lừa đảo kiểu này đang tăng mạnh vì khai thác lỗi con người, không phải lỗi kỹ thuật.Cách phòng ngừa đơn giản nhưng cực kỳ hiệu quảLuôn kiểm tra địa chỉ đầy đủ (42 ký tự cho Ethereum) – không chỉ đầu và cuối.  #BTC #ETH #sol

title: Circular financial system of hype: Inside AI’s self-financing machine.
subTitle:
OpenAI estimates spending $9b to maintain fashions going for walks earlier than salaries, rent, or research.
than salaries, rent, or research.
When Oracle Corp. introduced a multi-hundred-billion-dollar computing deal with OpenAI closing September, its inventory jumped 30-40 percentage in a single day. The $330 billion bounce in market cost was once large than Oracle’s whole income for the preceding decade. The organization later admitted it would lose cash on the contract.Nvidia pledged $100 billion to OpenAI whilst promoting it the very chips that spending would finance. Microsoft booked OpenAI’s compute payments as Azure income whilst reinvesting the proceeds into CoreWeave, any other OpenAI provider that additionally counts Nvidia as a shareholder. It feels like round financing on a planetary scale.Math doesn’t close
Start with the basics. OpenAI misplaced roughly $5 billion in 2024 on $3.7 billion in revenue. It’s estimated to spend $9 billion simply maintaining its fashions going for walks earlier than salaries, rent, or research. According to filings and investor projections, losses should attain $14 billion this 12 months and $44 billion cumulatively via 2028, and but its valuation sits at almost half of a trillion dollars. It is amongst the most treasured personal agencies on Earth, in spite of in no way turning a profit.The imbalance isn’t unique. Santiment Warned: The Bottom for Bitcoin Has Not Yet Formed!

Maksim Balashevich, the founder of Santiment, stated that the level of fear specific to the formation of a bottom in the crypto markets has not yet emerged, warning that downward movement in Bitcoin prices may continue.

In a YouTube video published on Friday, Balashevich emphasized that optimism is still strong across social media. He argued that this outlook is not conducive to a permanent bottom formation, expressing that Bitcoin could pull back towards the $75,000 level.

The $75,000 region is on the agenda: Excessive optimism overshadows bottom formation
Balashevich noted that the $75,000 level is technically a “very attractive” area, stating that it would not be surprising for the price to approach this level further.

The foundation of this cautious stance lies in the strong belief among investors that the recent pullback will come to an end soon. According to Balashevich, true market bottoms shape in an environment of widespread pessimism, fatigue, and fear rather than hope and optimism.

A separate report released by Santiment on the same day also highlighted a similar point. The report stated that the market has not yet feared enough to form a bottom.

Balashevich mentioned that expectations of a renewed rise are being discussed, particularly on online platforms where individual investors are concentrated, noting that macro developments such as interest rate decisions in Japan are fueling this optimism.

“The general belief is that those who are caught in the downturn will see a movement upwards from here. Frankly, these are not the statements I want to see,” he assessed.

🚨 A $50,000,000 Mistake: The Silent On-Chain Scam Every Crypto User Must Understand

A crypto whale just lost nearly $50 million in a highly sophisticated address poisoning attack — and the most alarming part?

There was no hack, no smart-contract bug, no private key leak.

This was purely a human-behavior exploit.

Here’s what happened 👇

The victim followed what many consider a safe habit:

First, a small test transfer of $USDT  to confirm the destination address.

That single action triggered the trap.

Within minutes, automated bots detected the transaction and generated a look-alike wallet address, matching the same starting and ending characters. The attacker then sent a tiny “dust” transaction from this fake address to pollute the victim’s transaction history.

Later, when the victim copied the address from history (instead of a trusted source), they unknowingly sent 49,999,950 USDT straight to the attacker.

💥 Gone in one transaction.

The stolen funds were quickly:

Swapped into $ETH 

Split across multiple wallets

Partially routed through mixers to obscure the trail

Recovery chances? Extremely low.

Why this scam is so dangerous

No technical exploit involved

Targets common user habits

Relies on visual similarity & convenience

Bots run 24/7, waiting patiently for one mistake

Even experienced users are vulnerable.

How to protect yourself

❌ Never copy addresses from transaction history

✅ Verify the entire address, not just first & last characters

✅ Use address whitelisting whenever possible

🚩 Treat dust transactions as warnings, not confirmations

Crypto doesn’t forgive small mistakes.

One careless click can cost a lifetime of gains.

Stay sharp. Stay paranoid. That’s real security in this market.

The Ethereum developers $ETH  revealed the name of the second upgrade scheduled for 2026. The hard fork is named Hegota — in honor of the city of Bogotá (the venue for Devcon) and the star Heze.
{future}(ETHUSDT)
The main improvement proposal for the update will be selected no earlier than February. The main candidate is the implementation of Verkle trees — a data structuring algorithm in the protocol, similar to Merkle trees. 
Attention will be given to mechanisms for expiration of history and state, as well as additional optimization of the execution level. The issue of network 'bloat' is becoming increasingly relevant for node operators.
Sharing new details, the network team has approved a stable schedule for the release of two hard forks per year. Before Hegota, the Glamsterdam update will be implemented. The latter implies possible integration of the following elements:

ePBS — separation of proposing and creating blocks at the protocol level to reduce centralization;
access lists — optimization of access to the network state;
gas repricing — adjustment of operation costs in EVM.
$ZEC $BCH #ETH

title: Ethereum Names “Hegota” as Its Next Major Upgrade, Shaping the 2026 Roadmap
subTitle:
Ethereum core developers have officially selected “Hegota” as the name of the network’s next upgrade, following Glamsterdam, further clarifying Ethereum’s 2026 development timeline as the protocol settles into its twice-yearly release schedule.
Hegota combines the execution-layer upgrade “Bogota”, continuing the tradition of Devcon host city names, with the consensus-layer upgrade “Heze,” which takes its name from a star. Developers emphasized that the headline Ethereum Improvement Proposal (EIP) for Hegota will not be chosen until February, while work on Glamsterdam remains ongoing.
The naming decision was finalized during Thursday’s All Core Developers Execution (ACDE) call, which marked the last meeting of the year. Developer discussions are set to resume on January 5, when the scope of Glamsterdam is expected to be finalized.

quoteContent.body: Crypto User Loses Nearly $50 Million USDT in Sophisticated On-Chain “Address Poisoning” Scam
quoteContent.title: Crypto User Loses Nearly $50 Million USDT in Sophisticated On-Chain “Address Poisoning” Scam
quoteContent.bodyTextOnly:
A crypto user has reportedly lost nearly 50 million USDT after falling victim to an advanced on-chain scam known as “address poisoning” — a deceptive technique that exploits user behavior rather than blockchain vulnerabilities.
According to Web3 security firm Antivirus, the incident began with what many traders consider a “safe habit”: sending a small test transaction. The victim initially transferred 50 USDT to verify the destination address before attempting to move the remaining balance.
However, within minutes, the attacker executed a carefully prepared trap.
How the Address Poisoning Attack Worked
After detecting the test transaction, the scammer quickly generated a wallet address that closely resembled the legitimate recipient’s address, especially in the first and last characters. Since most crypto wallets display addresses in shortened form (prefix + suffix), this visual similarity is often enough to deceive users.
To deepen the trap, the attacker sent a tiny amount of tokens (“dust”) to the victim’s wallet from the fake address. This “dust transaction” was deliberately designed to pollute the transaction history.
Believing the address to be correct, the victim later copied the address directly from transaction history — unknowingly selecting the attacker’s lookalike address — and transferred 49,999,950 USDT straight into the scammer’s wallet.
Why This Scam Is So Dangerous
Address poisoning scams do not exploit smart contract bugs, private keys, or cryptographic flaws. Instead, they rely entirely on human habits, particularly:
Copy–pasting wallet addresses
Verifying only the first and last characters
Trusting transaction history without manual confirmation
Automated bots continuously scan the blockchain for high-balance wallets, then send dust transactions en masse, patiently waiting for a single mistake. In this case, the mistake was catastrophic.
What Happened to the Stolen Funds?
On-chain data shows that the stolen USDT was quickly:
Swapped into ETH
Split and routed through multiple intermediary wallets
Partially funneled through Tornado Cash, a crypto mixing service sanctioned by U.S. authorities, in an attempt to obscure fund origins
These steps significantly reduce the chances of recovery and complicate any legal pursuit.
Victim’s On-Chain Ultimatum to the Hacker
In a rare move, the victim posted an on-chain message directly to the attacker, demanding the return of 98% of the stolen funds within 48 hours.
The message proposed allowing the hacker to keep $1 million USD as a so-called “white-hat bounty” if the remaining funds were returned. It also included a legal warning, stating that failure to comply would result in escalation through international law enforcement channels.
“This is your final opportunity to resolve this matter peacefully,” the message read.
“Failure to cooperate will result in criminal proceedings.”
At the time of writing, there is no confirmation that any funds have been returned.
Key Takeaway for Crypto Users
This incident is a brutal reminder that the weakest link in crypto security is often the user.
To reduce risk:
Never copy wallet addresses from transaction history
Always verify the entire address, not just the first and last characters
Use address whitelisting where possible
Treat unsolicited dust transactions as red flags, not confirmations
In crypto, one careless click can cost millions.

title: هجوم تصيّد بقيمة 50 مليون USDT يسلّط الضوء على ثغرة خطيرة في عرض العناوين
subTitle:
شهد مجتمع العملات الرقمية مؤخرًا حادثة أمنية خطيرة تمثلت في هجوم تصيّد (Phishing) أدى إلى خسارة 50 مليون USDT، ما دفع مؤسسة مجتمع إيثريوم إلى الخروج بتوصيات عاجلة لتفادي تكرار مثل هذه الحوادث مستقبلاً.
الحادثة لم تكن نتيجة اختراق تقني معقد، بل بسبب ممارسة شائعة وخطيرة في عرض عناوين المحافظ.
ما الذي حدث بالضبط؟
المهاجم قام بإنشاء عنوان محفظة يتطابق مع العنوان الحقيقي للضحية في أول وآخر ثلاثة أحرف.
وبسبب أن بعض المحافظ ومستكشفي البلوك تشين يعرضون العناوين بشكل مختصر باستخدام النقاط (…) مثل:
0xbaf4b1aF…B6495F8b5
فقد اعتقد الضحية أنه يرسل الأموال إلى العنوان الصحيح، بينما في الواقع تم تحويل 50 مليون USDT إلى عنوان مزيف متشابه.
تحذير رسمي من مؤسسة إيثريوم
ردًا على الحادثة، شددت مؤسسة مجتمع إيثريوم على ما يلي:
التوقف الفوري عن استخدام العناوين المختصرة
ضرورة عرض عنوان المحفظة كاملًا بدون إخفاء أي جزء
التأكيد على أن إخفاء أجزاء من العنوان يزيد من المخاطر بدل تقليلها
كما أوضحت أن بعض خيارات واجهة المستخدم (UI) في المحافظ الرقمية ومستكشفي البلوك تشين تمثل مشكلة أمنية حقيقية، لكنها قابلة للحل من خلال تحسين طريقة عرض العناوين.
لماذا هذا الأمر خطير؟
البلوك تشين لا يسمح باسترجاع المعاملات
أي خطأ في العنوان يعني خسارة نهائية للأموال
المهاجمون باتوا يعتمدون على التشابه البصري بدل الاختراق التقني
المستخدم هو الحلقة الأضعف عند غياب الوضوح
ما الدرس المستفاد؟
هذه الحادثة تؤكد أن:
الأمن لا يقتصر على العقود الذكية والتشفير
واجهة المستخدم قد تكون سببًا في خسائر ضخمة
التفاصيل الصغيرة مثل عرض العنوان كاملًا قد تحمي ملايين الدولارات
الخلاصة
هجوم الـ 50 مليون USDT هو تذكير قوي بأن الراحة البصرية لا يجب أن تأتي على حساب الأمان.
عرض عناوين المحافظ كاملة ليس خيارًا تجميليًا، بل ضرورة أمنية في عالم لا يعترف بالأخطاء.
احرص دائمًا على التحقق من العنوان كاملًا، فثانية انتباه قد توفر عليك خسارة لا يمكن تعويضها.
إذا رغبت، أستطيع:
تحويل المقال إلى نسخة قصيرة تحذيرية
أو استخراج نصائح أمان سريعة قابلة للنشر كمنشور منفصل على Binance Square

title: How to Survive the December Market? 5 Simple Strategies for the End of 2025
subTitle:
🎄 December 2025 – the market is throwing us a festive surprise! BTC hovering near $88k, memecoins in a light pump, altcoins slowly waking up after a long sleep. 
But how not to burn your portfolio before the holidays? Here are 5 simple strategies that actually work in this period:

1. Don't chase FOMO 
Seeing +20% on some altcoin and want to jump in? Skip it. December is full of fake breakouts and bull traps. Wait for a pullback or volume confirmation. I always wait for 2–3 candles on 4h.

2. The "50% profit = sell half" rule 
When a coin goes up 50–100%, sell half your position. December often brings 30–50% corrections after quick pumps. Take profit and sleep well.

3. Keep stablecoins ready for opportunities 
30–50% of portfolio in USDT/USDC. When the post-holiday dip comes (January loves to dump), you'll have cash for cheap buys. History shows Q1 after Christmas often gives great entries.

4. Daily DCA into BTC and ETH 
No matter the price – put in a fixed amount every day/week. In December the average price is often higher than in January. This is the safest strategy.

5. Holidays = go offline 
Most important: don't trade 24–26 December and 1 January. Market is thin, manipulation is high, emotions are wild. Take a break, eat pierogi (or whatever you celebrate with), and come back with a clear head.
